correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the vertices of KG(n,2) are edges on n labels; any selected disjoint pair ab,cd forces every other selected edge into {ac,ad,bc,bd}, giving a unique four-point support. Without disjoint pairs, a 2-uniform intersecting family is a star or triangle. Counting sizes 0,1,2 separately and the 12 three-edge,15 four-edge,6 five-edge,1 six-edge four-support families yields the displayed D_n. Adding any missing four-support edge preserves dissociation, and n>=5 complete stars have at least two neighbors disjoint from every outside pair, so precisely the claimed maximal sets survive (n=4 exceptional). Independent enumeration of all 2^6+2^10+2^15+2^21=2,131,008 subsets gives dissociation counts [64,261,747,1751] and maximal size distributions n=4 {6:1},n=5 {4:5,6:5},n=6 {5:6,6:15},n=7 {6:42}. This is finite corroboration of unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The 2021 Brešar–Dravec proposition already proves maximum size max(n-1,6) and the four-support restriction; these are explicitly excluded from new credit. The complete all-set polynomial and all inclusion-maximal sets including the purity n=4,7 classification and arbitrary cardinality gaps are not implied by that numerical maximum. Triangular/rook graph dissociation polynomials are for different adjacency graphs.

The 2021 maximum theorem and four-support bound must remain credited, not claimed as new.

value.rationale: An exact dissociation polynomial and complete list of inclusion-maximal sets solve natural enumerative and facet/purity questions for the classical Kneser family, not just recomputation of the known extremal dissociation number. The n=7 equality and n>=9 unbounded missing-size interval are structural phenomena a graph researcher can cite; proof is uniform in n.
